title: Candidate family — simplified format with student instructions
description: Fill one record per sourced candidate during collection. Preserve all source approaches, check validity, propose mechanism clusters, and defend at least two distinct valid routes. Tp and Tc are relative to selected clusters: Tp may change wording or numbers; Tc may be solved by another original cluster. Descriptions are instructions, not extra fields in records. Format validation does not establish mathematical validity or expert approval.

family_id.description: [NOW] Your unique ID for this candidate, for example "train_0057". Keep it stable while reviewing the same original problem; transformed versions belong inside this family, not in new source-family records.

file.description: [NOW] The source repository/file path or direct file URL. The prefilled path points to the released multi-approach dataset; replace it only when using another source.

problem_id.description: [NOW] The exact ID in the specified source file. For train.jsonl, use the record's "index" value, for example 57, not the row number. This is not an independently recovered upstream MATH ID.

source.description: [NOW] Where the original problem can be retrieved. Store only its file location and exact identifier.

collected_by.description: [NOW] The student who selected and assembled the candidate. Enter your name.

domain.description: [NOW] The problem's main mathematical subject, using your assigned domain name, for example "probability", "combinatorics", "geometry", or "algebra". Classify the problem, not the technique of one solution. These are team-assigned labels, not native labels in this file.

statement.description: [NOW] Copy the full original problem statement faithfully, including assumptions and mathematical notation. Do not replace it with a proposed transformed problem or silently repair it.

reference_answer.description: [NOW] Copy the source answer as a string. If a check disagrees with it, keep the source answer and explain the discrepancy in interpretation_notes and solution_check; do not silently overwrite it.

interpretation_notes.description: [NOW IF NEEDED] A list of ambiguities, implicit conventions, or source-answer issues that affect the mathematics, one string per issue. Explain any interpretation you use. Leave [] if there are no such notes; do not invent assumptions merely to make a solution work.

problem.description: [NOW] The unchanged source problem, its source answer, and any interpretation issues.

approach_id.description: [NOW] A local identifier such as "A1", "A2", or "A3", following the original source order. These IDs identify source plans within this family, not shared strategies across different problems.

name.description: [NOW] Copy the source approach's name. A different name alone does not establish a different mathematical approach.

core_idea.description: [NOW] Copy the source's core-idea description. Evaluate it in your checks rather than rewriting it to match a preferred cluster.

plan.description: [NOW] Copy the ordered source steps as a list of strings. Preserve errors or omissions in the source text; document corrections or completions in solution_check and validity_check.reason.

solution_check.description: [NOW] Write the mathematical evidence: a worked derivation, a precise error/counterexample, or the specific missing step. An answer or a claim of validity is not enough. Clearly label any completion or correction you add to the source plan.

status.description: [NOW] Use "valid" for a supported derivation; "invalid" for an identified error in the stated reasoning; "incomplete" when essential steps are missing; or "uncertain" when validity is unresolved. Leave null only before checking.

reason.description: [NOW] Explain the status, pointing to the decisive calculation, error, or missing justification. Distinguish a valid completion from a repair that changes faulty source reasoning. A valid plan can still belong to the same cluster as another.

validity_check.description: [NOW] Assess this plan's mathematical validity, separately from whether it differs from another approach.

approaches.description: [NOW] Include every source-listed approach in its original order, even if it is flawed or redundant. Duplicate this object for A2, A3, A4, and so on. A selected pair later does not permit dropping the others.

cluster_id.description: [NOW] A local ID such as "C1" or "C2". C1 in another problem is not automatically the same strategy. Keep IDs stable when later transformation proposals reference them.

approach_ids.description: [NOW] The IDs of approaches in this group, for example ["A1", "A3"]. Use only IDs present in approaches; do not place an approach in more than one group.

mechanism.description: [NOW] Define the shared solving route: its central mathematical justification, essential steps, and the conditions it relies on. Be more specific than 'use algebra'. This fixed definition is what Tp will preserve or Tc will challenge.

reason.description: [NOW] Explain the grouping. For merged plans, identify why their differences do not change the central reasoning. For a separate route, identify its distinctive mechanism. A singleton group alone does not prove distinctness; justify the separation in comparisons.

groups.description: [NOW] One object per supported mechanism cluster. Put valid approaches together when they have the same central route despite execution or presentation changes. Keep genuinely different routes separate. Do not count invalid or incomplete plans as extra valid clusters.

approach_id.description: [NOW IF NEEDED] The existing approach ID that is not placed in a group, for example "A3".

reason.description: [NOW IF NEEDED] Explain the precise obstacle: mathematical error, missing derivation, or unresolved relation to another mechanism. A valid but unassigned plan is not automatically a new cluster.

unassigned.description: [NOW IF NEEDED] List every plan that cannot yet be placed in a supported group, with an approach_id and reason. This includes invalid/incomplete plans and valid plans whose distinctness remains unresolved. Use [] if all approaches are confidently grouped.

approach_ids.description: [NOW] Exactly two distinct existing approach IDs, for example ["A1", "A2"].

verdict.description: [NOW] Use "same" for the same central route; "different" for a substantive change in mathematical reasoning; "uncertain" for an unresolved boundary between executable routes; or "insufficient_evidence" when flawed or underspecified reasoning prevents the comparison.

reason.description: [NOW] Identify the decisive shared step or difference. Notation, wording, reordering, or an equivalent algebraic cleanup alone does not justify 'different'. Keep the verdict consistent with the groups.

comparisons.description: [NOW] Record pairwise evidence for the grouping. Provide enough comparisons to justify your merges, splits, selected distinct pair, and unresolved cases without repeating identical explanations.

clustering.description: [NOW] Your proposed grouping by central mathematical reasoning. Assess the plans rather than adopting the source's uniqueness count. Every source approach must appear in exactly one group or in unassigned.

recommendation.description: [NOW] Use "shortlist" when at least two valid, genuinely distinct routes are supported; "hold" when more evidence or repair is needed; or "reject" when the current candidate should not be retained. Leave null before making a recommendation.

distinct_approach_pair.description: [NOW] Exactly two valid approach IDs from different supported groups that best demonstrate the selection criterion, for example ["A1", "A2"]. Keep all approaches in the record. Use [] when no defensible pair has been established; do not supply just one ID.

reason.description: [NOW] Explain why the evidence supports your recommendation. Identify the strongest pair and central distinction, or the blocker for a held/rejected candidate. An unresolved Tc idea alone does not invalidate a source problem's two-approach qualification.

selection.description: [NOW] Your recommendation about retaining the whole original problem as a candidate, based on the validity and clustering evidence. This is not expert approval.

status.description: [IDEAS NOW] Use "not_started", "idea", or "blocked" during collection. "idea" means proposed, not established. "blocked" means an identified obstacle, explained below. Later, "draft" means a developed but unvalidated variant; "validated" requires explicit mathematical review, not a JSON-format check.

target_cluster_ids.description: [IDEAS NOW] The source cluster you intend to preserve, normally a single ID such as ["C2"]. Reference clustering.groups, not an approach ID. If you intentionally target several clusters, justify preservation for each. For the comparison pair, Tc should target the same selected cluster.

idea.description: [IDEAS NOW] Describe the exact proposed surface or parameter edit. State what changes and what stays fixed. A complete transformed statement is not required yet. Leave null only when no concrete idea is available, and explain the obstacle in open_questions.

reason.description: [IDEAS NOW] Explain why the targeted mechanism should remain applicable: identify its conditions and map the essential steps to the proposed edit. A numerical change is not automatically preserving. Write an expectation rather than claiming a proof you have not supplied.

expected_cluster_id.description: [IDEAS NOW] The selected source cluster expected to solve the variant, normally the same ID as the single target, for example "C2". Use null if not yet established. If several targets are listed, name a primary one here and discuss the others in reason.

open_questions.description: [IDEAS NOW] List remaining checks or blockers, such as parameter validity, unchanged assumptions, or a required derivation. Use [] only if no questions are currently identified; an empty list is not validation.

statement.description: [LATER] The exact full transformed problem statement, including domains and assumptions. It must be understandable without reading the proposed edit.

reference_answer.description: [LATER] The checked answer to this transformed problem, stored as a string; it need not equal the source answer.

approach.description: [LATER] A clear name or existing cluster ID for the route actually used. Describe a new route explicitly rather than implying that it is a verified source cluster.

steps.description: [LATER] The ordered steps of a complete derivation, one string per step. Include essential justifications and assumptions rather than only the final answer.

worked_solutions.description: [LATER] A list of checked solution objects for the variant. For Tp, include a solution using the target mechanism; for Tc, include a valid alternative and explain target failure in the proposal's reason.

method.description: [LATER] How the transformation was constructed: the actual edit rule, manual steps, prompt, or script used. State what was done, not a planned method.

variant.description: [LATER] Leave null for the collection stage. Later this holds the developed statement, checked reference answer, worked solutions, and construction method. Do not fill it with an invented completed variant.

Tp.description: [IDEAS NOW] Mechanism-preserving ideas. Wording, names/context, notation, representation, and numerical parameters may change; the answer may change too. The selected mechanism's conditions and essential steps must still work. Other original approaches need not all be preserved.

status.description: [IDEAS NOW] Use "not_started", "idea", or "blocked" during collection. A plausible edit is only an "idea". Use "blocked" if the target still works or no convincing change is available, and state why. Reserve "draft" and "validated" for development and explicit mathematical validation later.

target_cluster_ids.description: [IDEAS NOW] The selected source cluster intended to fail, normally a single ID such as ["C2"]. It need not include every source cluster. If several clusters are intentionally targeted, justify failure for each. Pair with Tp targeting the same fixed mechanism.

idea.description: [IDEAS NOW] Describe the proposed small edit and what makes the problem still look similar. Do not simply request 'use another method' on the unchanged problem. A new answer or a longer calculation alone does not establish a mechanism change.

reason.description: [IDEAS NOW] Identify the exact assumption or essential step that should fail, and explain why ordinary substitutions or routine execution adjustments do not rescue the fixed target route. Suggest how a different route could solve the variant. Another route working is not, by itself, evidence that the target fails.

expected_cluster_id.description: [IDEAS NOW] An existing source cluster expected to solve the changed problem, for example "C1" when the target is C2. It may be another original cluster. Use null if the alternative is unknown or not yet an existing cluster; describe a proposed new route in idea/reason rather than inventing an undefined ID. For a blocked proposal, recording the same cluster as the target can document why the edit failed.

open_questions.description: [IDEAS NOW] List unsettled mathematical checks: whether the target can adapt, whether the edit stays sufficiently similar, whether the alternative works, and any ambiguity in strategy granularity. The rule allowing another original cluster to remain valid is already agreed and is not an open question.

statement.description: [LATER] The exact full transformed problem statement, including domains and assumptions. It must be understandable without reading the proposed edit.

reference_answer.description: [LATER] The checked answer to this transformed problem, stored as a string; it need not equal the source answer.

approach.description: [LATER] A clear name or existing cluster ID for the route actually used. Describe a new route explicitly rather than implying that it is a verified source cluster.

steps.description: [LATER] The ordered steps of a complete derivation, one string per step. Include essential justifications and assumptions rather than only the final answer.

worked_solutions.description: [LATER] A list of checked solution objects for the variant. For Tp, include a solution using the target mechanism; for Tc, include a valid alternative and explain target failure in the proposal's reason.

method.description: [LATER] How the transformation was constructed: the actual edit rule, manual steps, prompt, or script used. State what was done, not a planned method.

variant.description: [LATER] Leave null for the collection stage. Later store the exact changed statement, checked answer, alternative worked solution(s), and construction method. Its correctness and target failure still need mathematical review.

Tc.description: [IDEAS NOW] Mechanism-changing ideas. Keep the setup recognizably similar while changing an assumption, constraint, parameter, or goal that makes the selected mechanism no longer applicable as a complete solving route. Another original cluster may still solve the variant; no entirely new approach is required.

transformations.description: [IDEAS NOW] Proposals relative to selected source clusters, not all original approaches. For a paired Tp/Tc proposal, use the same fixed target mechanism. Keep each cluster definition fixed while designing edits. Complete statements, solutions, generation methods, and expert validation come later.

reviewer.description: [EXPERT ONLY] Name of the person who actually performed the expert review. Leave null until that review occurs.

decision.description: [EXPERT ONLY] Keep "pending" until expert review. The reviewer may later use "accept", "revise", or "reject" for the record at its current stage. Accepting a source candidate does not automatically validate its transformation proposals.

comments.description: [EXPERT ONLY] Leave null for the student submission. The expert records approval scope, corrections, and unresolved issues, referring to approach or cluster IDs where helpful.

expert_review.description: [EXPERT ONLY] Mayssa's separate mathematical review of the candidate. Students leave the defaults unchanged. A shortlist recommendation or collected_by='Mayssa' is not an expert approval.
